name: Pebble Beach Golf Links
blurb: Jack Neville and Douglas Grant’s 1919 links on the cliffs above Carmel Bay — the small greens of the 7th and the long 18th along the shore.

name: Spyglass Hill
blurb: Robert Trent Jones Sr., 1966: five holes in the sand dunes by the ocean, then up into the Del Monte Forest.

name: Torrey Pines South
blurb: The city of San Diego’s clifftop course above the Pacific, a U.S. Open venue.

name: Bethpage Black
blurb: A.W. Tillinghast’s public-course brute; the sign at the first tee warns that it is recommended only for highly skilled golfers.

name: TPC Sawgrass Stadium
blurb: Pete Dye’s 1980 stadium course, built for spectators — and for the island green at the 17th.

name: Chambers Bay
blurb: A fescue links in a former sand-and-gravel quarry on Puget Sound, by Robert Trent Jones Jr.

name: Whistling Straits
blurb: Pete Dye’s shaped links along two miles of Lake Michigan shoreline, with bunkers beyond counting.

name: Pinehurst No. 2
blurb: Donald Ross’s crowned, turtle-backed greens and sandy waste areas.

name: Harbour Town Golf Links
blurb: Pete Dye and Jack Nicklaus, 1969: tight, tree-lined, and finishing at the lighthouse.

name: The Ocean Course
blurb: Pete Dye’s course in the dunes along the Atlantic, exposed to the wind on every hole.

name: Bandon Dunes
blurb: David McLay Kidd’s 1999 links on the cliffs of the Oregon coast.

name: Pacific Dunes
blurb: Tom Doak’s routing through the dunes above the Pacific.

name: Erin Hills
blurb: Glacial hills and fescue in the Kettle Moraine, a U.S. Open venue.

name: TPC Harding Park
blurb: A municipal course wrapped around Lake Merced, lined with cypress.

name: Cog Hill No. 2
blurb: The Ravines: Dubsdread’s neighbour, shorter and rolling.
